To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new loss function and a new training procedure for sequence to sequence models with continuous outputs that (i) are upto 2.4x faster to train than the state-of-the art models, (ii) perform on par with the best models on translation quality, and (iii) produce errors that are more meaningful than those produced by the softmax based models.
we can train and evaluate sequence-to-sequence neural machine translation models with large vocabularies, and we can train them upto 2.3x faster than the state-of-the art models.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new class of sequence to sequence models that are more efficient than the state-of-the art models.
the following question: can we replace the softmax layer in neural machine translation models with a continuous layer?
the design of sequence-to-se-quence models with continuous output distributions that are faster to train than the softmax-based models while being able to handle large vocabularies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the softmax function is a bottleneck for the training and inference in sequence-to-sequence language models and can be replaced by a continuous embedding layer with minimal loss in translation quality, but with a significant speed-up in training, and with the potential of handling very large and unbounded vocabularies.
the proposed method is a viable alternative for softmax in neural machine translation and can be extended for other language generation tasks.
we have proposed a novel technique to replace the softmax layer with an embedding layer in sequence to sequence models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel probabilistic objective function for sequence-to-sequence modeling with continuous outputs, and show that it can be trained and used for inference in an end-to-end manner, without any post-processing.
we are able to train faster and larger sequence-to-sequence neural models with a continuous embedding output.
the proposed model is faster, more accurate, and more interpretable than existing models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the softmax function can be completely replaced with a continuous embedding function without any loss in performance.
the softmax layer is not a necessity for sequence-to-sequence learning, and that the softmax can be replaced by a more efficient and more accurate layer, which is the continuous output layer.
we can train sequence-to-sequence neural models with continuous embeddings, which are faster to train and faster at inference, while achieving competitive results on the task of translation.
